description:
Follow-up to fz-qe0, which removed the dominant term (the recursive-group
reachability walk stepping into settled products: 21.9M node visits -> 9.9K,
run 12.2s -> 3.9s).

The fixture is still ~3.15s debug on a fast dev machine, which by
[[feedback_tiny_fixture_slowness_is_correctness]] is still excess work for a
24-line program: a tiny fixture measured in seconds means repeated work, not hard
work.

## Measured (fz-qe0 HEAD, --log-telemetry, interp lane)

Time attributed to the gap preceding each product settle:

    executable_facts          533 settles    429 ms
    runtime_demand              3 settles    343 ms
    callable_construction    2625 settles    229 ms   (was 6704 ms)
    transport_shape          2702 settles    159 ms
    abi_executable            242 settles     65 ms

plus ~0.9s inside drive jobs, of which AnalyzeActivation is 921 spans / 791 ms.

## THE SIGNAL IS THE COUNT, NOT THE COST

242 executables but 2625 callable_construction and 2702 transport_shape
settlements -- about 11 of each per executable. Each is now cheap, so the wall
clock no longer screams, but the POPULATION is the thing to explain: either those
are genuinely distinct positions, or products are re-settling (churn). Establish
which BEFORE optimizing anything -- if it is churn it belongs to the
fz-go4.18.28 transport-monolith / partial-publication family and the fix is
upstream.

921 AnalyzeActivation spans for this fixture is also worth a census against the
activation inventory.

FIRST STEP: count DISTINCT ProductKeys settled per kind versus total settlements.
Equal => genuine population, look at why position count is 11x executable count.
Unequal => churn, and the re-settle triggers are the lead.

## Re-measure first: the input may have shrunk

fz-6gb landed after these numbers were taken and cut executable fanout ~5x on
lambda-heavy programs (32 distinct lambdas: 233 executables -> 45). This fixture
has 24 lambda call sites, so its 242 executables and the per-executable ratios
above may be materially different now. Re-run the telemetry census before
drawing conclusions from the table.

## The budget is no longer the detector

The fixture's `timeout.run_secs` / `timeout.interp_secs` were 6s specifically to
keep this visible. That did not survive contact with CI -- a wall-clock budget
calibrated on dev hardware exceeded its cap on EVERY CI run of the
fz-go4.1..fz-f98.24 stack, because the runners are slower and run under
`llvm-cov` instrumentation. The caps are now 20s hang backstops, documented as
deliberately too loose to notice a regression (main 120c86192).

So DO NOT rely on the fixture budget to catch a regression here, and do not
tighten it again -- that was tried and it produced a permanently red CI signal
that everyone learned to ignore. The replacement detector is a machine
independent work-count ceiling asserting the settlement volume above:
fz-f98.23.
title: enum_predicate_search compiles for 3.15s: 2625 callable_construction settlements for 242 executables
